quests.partialSentence: It's been ten years since we ____ each other in person.
quests.hint: After 'since', the clause names a finished moment in the past.
quests.explanation: In 'It's been ... since ...', the main clause uses the present perfect and the 'since' clause uses the simple past for the finished event. The last meeting is a single completed point, so 'saw' is used.
quests.grammarFocus: Present Perfect vs Past Simple in Since-Clauses

quests.partialSentence: Ever since the merger, our workload ____ steadily.
quests.hint: 'Ever since' links a past starting point to today.
quests.explanation: A change that began at a past point and continues into the present takes the present perfect. The simple past would suggest the growth is over.

quests.partialSentence: The company ____ its prices twice since January, and customers are noticing.
quests.hint: Two events in an unfinished period that still matter now.
quests.explanation: 'Since January' opens a period that runs to now, and the price rises have present consequences. That combination calls for the present perfect.

quests.partialSentence: By the time the ambulance arrived, the crowd ____.
quests.hint: Which action finished first?
quests.explanation: 'By the time' + simple past signals a deadline, and anything completed before it takes the past perfect. The crowd was gone before the ambulance came.

quests.partialSentence: I had never seen snow before I ____ to Canada.
quests.hint: 'Before' connects two past events. Which one is the later one?
quests.explanation: With 'before', the later event is in the simple past, and the earlier state takes the past perfect. Moving to Canada is the later point, so it does not need 'had'.

quests.partialSentence: Tom looked exhausted; he ____ for nearly twenty hours.
quests.hint: The tiredness in the past was caused by something already in progress.
quests.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows a longer activity that led up to a past moment and explains it. 'Nearly twenty hours' stresses duration.

quests.partialSentence: By next June, I ____ my degree.
quests.hint: 'By next June' marks a deadline in the future.
quests.explanation: The future perfect (will have + participle) talks about something finished before a future deadline. 'By' is the usual signal.

quests.partialSentence: This time tomorrow, we ____ on a beach in Goa.
quests.hint: The sentence pictures a moment in progress in the future.
quests.explanation: The future continuous describes an action in progress at a specific future time. 'This time tomorrow' is the classic signal.

quests.partialSentence: Don't call me at ten tomorrow; I ____ to the board.
quests.hint: The person will be busy at that exact time.
quests.explanation: The future continuous explains why someone will be unavailable, since the action is in progress at that moment.

quests.partialSentence: If we had left ten minutes earlier, we ____ the train.
quests.hint: The if-clause describes something that did not happen in the past.
quests.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + participle. It pictures a different past and its imagined result.

quests.partialSentence: She wouldn't have missed the deadline if she ____ the email.
quests.hint: Focus on the if-clause, which comes second here.
quests.explanation: The if-clause of a third conditional needs the past perfect, regardless of position. The main clause already shows 'wouldn't have missed'.

quests.partialSentence: If the store ____ me a refund, I wouldn't have written that review.
quests.hint: Never use 'would have' in the if-clause.
quests.explanation: 'Would have' belongs in the result clause only. The if-clause of an unreal past uses the past perfect: 'had offered'.

quests.partialSentence: If I had taken that job in Pune, I ____ in a different city now.
quests.hint: The condition is in the past but the result is true now.
quests.explanation: A mixed conditional links a past condition (past perfect) to a present result (would + base). 'Now' tells you the result is present.

quests.partialSentence: If she weren't so stubborn, she ____ the problem earlier.
quests.hint: The condition describes a present trait; the result is in the past.
quests.explanation: A present condition ('weren't so stubborn') can lead to an imagined past result ('would have solved'). This is the reverse mixed pattern.

quests.partialSentence: If we had backed up the files, we ____ so stressed right now.
quests.hint: 'Right now' fixes the time of the result.
quests.explanation: The past condition is unreal, but its result affects the present, so we use 'would(n't) be'. 'Right now' rules out 'have been'.

quests.partialSentence: I wish I ____ how to cook; ordering food every night is expensive.
quests.hint: The wish concerns a present situation.
quests.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about the present. Nothing in the sentence points to the past.

quests.partialSentence: If only I ____ the receipt; I can't return this shirt without it.
quests.hint: The regret is about something already done.
quests.explanation: For regret about the past, 'if only' takes the past perfect. The missing receipt is a consequence of not keeping it.

quests.partialSentence: She wishes she ____ harder for the entrance exam last year.
quests.hint: 'Last year' places the regret in the past.
quests.explanation: Wishes about the past use the past perfect. 'Last year' rules out present or future forms.

quests.partialSentence: All visitors ____ to sign in at the front desk.
quests.hint: Visitors receive the requirement; they don't create it.
quests.explanation: The passive (be + participle) is used when the receiver of the action is the focus. Notices often use it to sound official.

quests.partialSentence: The bridge ____ in 1932 and is still in daily use.
quests.hint: The builder is not important, and the year is in the past.
quests.explanation: 'In 1932' requires a past form, and the bridge is the receiver, so we use the past passive 'was built'.

quests.partialSentence: Cash ____ at the entrance; please use the card machine.
quests.hint: Cash cannot accept anything itself.
quests.explanation: Because cash receives the action, we need a passive verb. The negative is 'isn't accepted'.

quests.partialSentence: The road ____ this week, so expect delays.
quests.hint: The work is happening now, around this period.
quests.explanation: The present continuous passive (is being + participle) describes ongoing work done to something.

quests.partialSentence: Your application ____ by a panel by the end of the month.
quests.hint: Future deadline + passive.
quests.explanation: The future perfect passive (will have been + participle) shows something finished before a deadline.

quests.partialSentence: This form ____ in black ink.
quests.hint: A modal in the passive keeps 'be'.
quests.explanation: Modal passive follows the pattern modal + be + participle.

quests.partialSentence: The meeting has been rescheduled, but nobody told us who ____ it.
quests.hint: The question word is the subject of the clause.
quests.explanation: In 'who + verb', the question word is the doer, so the verb is active. 'Was rescheduled' would need the meeting as subject.

quests.partialSentence: Our website ____ by a cyber attack last night, and the team is still investigating.
quests.hint: 'By a cyber attack' shows the doer, so the website is the receiver.
quests.explanation: When the subject receives the action and the doer is introduced with 'by', use the passive.

quests.partialSentence: Sorry for the delay in replying; your message ____ into our system.
quests.hint: The message can't log itself.
quests.explanation: A message cannot perform the action of logging, so a passive verb is needed.

quests.partialSentence: Last Monday, the landlord told us that the repairs ____ finished by Friday.
quests.hint: In reported speech after a past verb, 'will' shifts.
quests.explanation: After a past reporting verb like 'told', 'will' usually moves back to 'would'. Passive 'would be finished' completes the structure.

quests.partialSentence: 'I've never been to Kerala,' Marta said. She said she ____ never been to Kerala.
quests.hint: Present perfect backshifts in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Have' + participle becomes 'had' + participle when reported after a past verb.

quests.partialSentence: 'I can't open this file,' he said. He said he ____ open the file.
quests.hint: Modals often shift back in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Can' generally becomes 'could' after a past reporting verb.
